Summary: Deuteronomy 23:7 forbids abhorring an Edomite: 'for he is thy brother.' Edom descends from Esau, Jacob's brother, and kinship limits enmity even after Edom's hostility.
Commandment: Do not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother.
Application: Kinship tempers enmity: even a hostile neighbour who is a brother is not to be abhorred. The admission rule that follows — their children of the third generation may enter the assembly — shows enmity with an end date. Debated: how far these assembly-admission provisions carry into the church is genuinely disputed — this row does not settle it.
Purpose: To protect the weaker party at each family step (Deuteronomy 21-25). Debated: the divorce certificate is read by Jesus as concession to hardness of heart, not God's design (Matthew 19:8), and levirate marriage ended, while creation marriage itself is reaffirmed. The site does not settle a single duration for this cluster because its parts do not share one fate.
